<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="a2a"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## A2A (Agent2Agent) {#a2a}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

An open protocol through which agents built on different frameworks discover
each other's capabilities and exchange tasks and messages.

**In practice.** A planning agent reads a data agent's Agent Card and
delegates a report as a tracked task.

**Watch for.** Interoperability does not establish trust: authentication,
authorization and task limits remain the deployer's responsibility.

**Related concepts:**

</p>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="agent"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## AI agent {#agent}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A system in which a model chooses tools or steps to pursue a task within
configured boundaries.

**In practice.** Inspect an incident, request a permitted log lookup and
propose the next step.

**Watch for.** Model output is not authority: software must enforce
permissions and approval.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="aiops"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## AIOps {#aiops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Use AI to assist operations, such as alert correlation, incident investigation

**In practice.** Connect a latency alert with traces and a recent deployment

**Watch for.** Correlation is not proof of cause; remediation needs scoped

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="airflow"

## Apache Airflow {#airflow}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Coordinate workflows defined as code, including dependencies, schedules,
retries and task state.

**In practice.** Run extraction, validation and reporting in dependency order
and inspect failed tasks.

**Watch for.** It is an orchestrator, not a per-event streaming engine.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="kafka"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Apache Kafka {#kafka}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

A distributed event-streaming platform with partitioned logs that producers
write and consumers can replay.

**In practice.** Publish order events so inventory and analytics can consume
them independently.

**Watch for.** Ordering is per partition, not global; retention and delivery
semantics need deliberate configuration.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="backfill"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Backfill {#backfill}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Recomputing or loading data for a past period, for example after fixing a
transformation or adding a column.

**In practice.** After correcting a currency bug, rerun the daily revenue
model for the last 90 partitions.

**Watch for.** A backfill must be idempotent and bounded: overwrite whole
partitions and limit its load on shared engines.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Idempotency](#idempotency) ·
[Batch processing](#batch) ·
[Apache Airflow](#airflow) ·
[dbt](#dbt) ·

</p>

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="backoff"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Backoff {#backoff}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Delay successive retries to reduce pressure on a failing dependency; jitter
spreads synchronized clients.

**In practice.** Try again after progressively longer bounded delays, with a
total retry budget.

**Watch for.** More retries can amplify an outage. Retry only eligible
failures and make side effects safe.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Idempotency](#idempotency) ·
[Circuit breaker](#circuit-breaker) ·
[Dead-letter queue](#dlq)

</p>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="batch"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Batch processing {#batch}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Process a bounded collection of data as a job, rather than treating it as an
endless flow.

**In practice.** Calculate yesterday's sales from a closed set of orders.

**Watch for.** Scheduling frequency and job duration determine how long
readers wait for new results.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="cdc"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Change data capture {#cdc}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Turn database changes into events that downstream consumers can process
incrementally.

**In practice.** Propagate inserts, updates and deletes from an operational
database to an analytical system.

**Watch for.** Snapshots, replay, deletes and schema changes require explicit
consumer behavior.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="circuit-breaker"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Circuit breaker {#circuit-breaker}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Temporarily stop calls after enough failures, then admit limited probes to
check recovery.

**In practice.** Open a circuit during a persistent dependency outage and test
it after a cooldown.

**Watch for.** It does not repair the dependency and can delay recovery if
thresholds are poorly chosen.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Backoff](#backoff) ·
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Site reliability engineering (SRE)](#sre)

</p>

Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/circuit-breaker)

[Link to this definition](#circuit-breaker)

</section>

## ClickHouse {#clickhouse}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

A column-oriented SQL database designed for analytical queries over large
volumes of data.

**In practice.** Aggregate event histories to power an operational dashboard.

**Watch for.** An analytical serving layer needs its own ingestion, retention
and recovery design; it does not replace every transactional database.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="compaction"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Compaction {#compaction}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Rewriting many small data files into fewer files near a target size, without
changing the table's rows.

**In practice.** Five-minute streaming commits leave 11 MiB files; a nightly
rewrite merges each hourly partition into one 512 MiB file.

**Watch for.** Compaction commits a new snapshot; the small files stay on
storage until older snapshots expire.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[Table snapshot and time travel](#snapshot) ·
[Streaming](#streaming) ·
[Object storage](#object-storage)

</p>

## Data lineage {#lineage}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Recorded relationships between datasets, jobs and runs that explain where data
came from and how it changed.

**In practice.** Trace a dashboard field back to the job and source dataset
that produced it.

**Watch for.** Lineage coverage can be incomplete; a dependency graph does not

## DataOps {#dataops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Collaborative practices that improve delivery and operation of analytical data

**In practice.** Validate a pipeline change with representative data before

**Watch for.** An orchestrator alone cannot replace ownership, quality

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="dlq"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Dead-letter queue {#dlq}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

A separate destination for messages that could not be processed within the
configured attempt limit.

**In practice.** Quarantine an invalid event after repeated failures and
inspect it before replay.

**Watch for.** Moving a message to a DLQ is not successful processing;
retention and replay need an owner.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**

[Idempotency](#idempotency) ·
[Apache Kafka](#kafka)

</p>

## DevOps {#devops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Shared practices and responsibility across software delivery and operation,
supported by automation and feedback.

**In practice.** The team that ships a service also uses incident feedback to
improve its delivery process.

**Watch for.** Renaming a team or installing a CI server does not establish
shared ownership.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="devsecops"

## DevSecOps {#devsecops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Integrate security practices and shared responsibility throughout software

**In practice.** Review threat assumptions, verify dependencies and test

**Watch for.** A scanner passing does not establish secure design; exceptions,

## DuckDB {#duckdb}

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="durable-execution"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Durable execution {#durable-execution}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Workflow execution whose progress is recorded, so it resumes after crashes,
deployments or long waits without repeating completed steps.

**In practice.** An approval workflow waits three days for a person and, after
a restart, continues at the next step.

**Watch for.** Steps with external side effects still need idempotency, and
code changes must stay compatible with running histories.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Idempotency](#idempotency) ·
[AI agent](#agent) ·

</p>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="embedding"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Embedding {#embedding}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A fixed-length vector that a model assigns to text, images or other data, so
that similar meaning ends up close together.

**In practice.** Two support tickets about a failed payment get nearby vectors
even when they share no words.

**Watch for.** Vectors from different models, versions or dimensions are not
comparable; changing the model means re-embedding the corpus.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Vector search](#vector-search) ·
[RAG](#rag) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation)

</p>

embeddings](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/embeddings)

[Link to this definition](#embedding)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="error-budget"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Error budget {#error-budget}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

The unreliability an SLO allows over its window: one minus the target, applied
to eligible requests or measured time.

**In practice.** A 99.9% target over 10 million monthly requests allows 10,000
failed requests.

**Watch for.** An exhausted budget is a signal to prioritize reliability work,
not an automatic penalty; partial windows need care.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Site reliability engineering (SRE)](#sre) ·
[Observability](#observability) ·
[Tail latency (p95/p99)](#tail-latency)

</p>

risk](https://sre.google/sre-book/embracing-risk/)

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="evaluation"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Evaluation {#evaluation}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A defined set of tasks and scoring rules used to inspect system behavior,
including failures.

**In practice.** Check task completion and unauthorized actions separately on
a held-out test set.

**Watch for.** A high aggregate score can hide dangerous failures; model
judges also need calibration.

[LLMOps](#llmops)

## FinOps {#finops}

## GitOps {#gitops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="hybrid-attention"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Hybrid attention {#hybrid-attention}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A model design that interleaves full-attention layers with linear-attention
layers whose recurrent state does not grow with context.

**In practice.** Qwen3.8 keeps a KV cache in one layer of every four; the
other three hold a fixed state per request.

**Watch for.** The saving applies to the cache, not the weights; long-context
recall and runtime support vary by model and engine.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[KV cache](#kv-cache) ·
[Mixture of experts (MoE)](#mixture-of-experts) ·
[Quantization](#quantization)

</p>

2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06464)

[Link to this definition](#hybrid-attention)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="idempotency"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Idempotency {#idempotency}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Repeating the same operation has the same intended effect as performing it
once.

**In practice.** Reuse an operation identifier when retrying an order creation
after a timeout.

**Watch for.** The key, scope and retention window matter; a timeout does not
prove the first attempt failed.

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="kv-cache"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## KV cache {#kv-cache}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Stored attention keys and values from prior tokens, reused during
autoregressive decoding.

**In practice.** Reuse the prompt cache while producing each subsequent token.

**Watch for.** Memory grows with sequence length and concurrency; hybrid
models cache only their full-attention layers, and layout depends on the
runtime.

## Lakehouse {#lakehouse}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

An analytical architecture combining lake-style storage with table management

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="landing-zone"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## Landing zone {#landing-zone}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

A prepared multi-account or multi-project cloud environment with baseline
identity, networking, logging and security guardrails for new workloads.

**In practice.** A new project inherits central logging, a shared network and
organization policies when it is created.

**Watch for.** It is a starting baseline, not a finished security posture; its
guardrails need owners, exceptions and change control.

**Related concepts:**
[VPC](#vpc) ·
[Infrastructure as code](#iac) ·
[Zero trust](#zero-trust) ·
[DevSecOps](#devsecops)

</p>

design](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/landing-zones)

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="llmops"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## LLMOps {#llmops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Lifecycle practices for releasing, evaluating and operating applications built
around language models.

**In practice.** Version prompts and retrieval data, evaluate a release and
observe its latency, cost and failures.

**Watch for.** A model benchmark does not validate the application's tools,
permissions or real user tasks.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[MLOps](#mlops) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation) ·
[KV cache](#kv-cache) ·

</p>

Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/generative-ai-lens/generative-ai-lens.html)

[Link to this definition](#llmops)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="mcp"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## MCP {#mcp}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A protocol through which AI applications discover and interact with tools,
resources and prompts exposed by servers.

**In practice.** Expose a read-only catalog tool through a server with
explicit access controls.

**Watch for.** Protocol compatibility does not grant permission or make tool
output trustworthy.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**

[A2A (Agent2Agent)](#a2a) ·

</p>

Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="medallion"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Medallion architecture {#medallion}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Organize data by refinement: bronze retains raw input, silver validates it and
gold serves a use case.

**In practice.** Preserve incoming orders, validate identifiers, then publish
a revenue summary.

**Watch for.** Layer names are a design convention, not proof of data quality
or a requirement to copy every dataset three times.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse) ·
[dbt](#dbt) ·
[Data lineage](#lineage)

</p>

architecture](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/lakehouse/medallion)

[Link to this definition](#medallion)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="mixture-of-experts"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Mixture of experts (MoE) {#mixture-of-experts}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

A model layer that routes each token to a few expert sub-networks, so only
part of the parameters computes each token.

**In practice.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next holds 180B parameters but activates about
6B per token.

**Watch for.** Every expert stays in memory: the active share lowers compute
and bandwidth per token, not resident weight memory.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Quantization](#quantization) ·
[KV cache](#kv-cache) ·
[Hybrid attention](#hybrid-attention) ·
[Prefill and decode](#prefill-decode)

</p>

[Read the source · Shazeer et al., ICLR
2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06538)

[Link to this definition](#mixture-of-experts)

[Try it: Compare resident and active weights](projects/tools.md#interactive-llm-calculator)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="mlops"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## MLOps {#mlops}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Practices for delivering and operating ML systems across code, data, training,
deployment and monitoring.

**In practice.** Version a model with its training data references, evaluation
results and rollback artifact.

**Watch for.** Automating deployment does not ensure model quality or detect
every change in production data.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[LLMOps](#llmops) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation) ·
[DevOps](#devops)

</p>

[Read the source · Google Cloud Architecture
Center](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/mlops-continuous-delivery-and-automation-pipelines-in-machine-learning)

[Link to this definition](#mlops)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="multi-agent"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Multi-agent systems {#multi-agent}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Several agents cooperate with distinct responsibilities, context or
permissions in one workflow.

**In practice.** A coordinator requests a report from a data agent and a
reviewer checks its sources.

**Watch for.** Additional agents increase coordination, latency and failure
paths; they do not guarantee better answers.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[AI agent](#agent) ·
[A2A (Agent2Agent)](#a2a) ·
[MCP](#mcp) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation)

</p>

[Read the source · Google ADK · workflows](https://adk.dev/workflows/)

[Link to this definition](#multi-agent)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="object-lock"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## Object Lock (WORM) {#object-lock}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

A storage setting that makes an object version immutable for a retention
period: write once, read many.

**In practice.** Backups are written with a 30-day lock, so neither ransomware
nor an operator mistake can delete them.

**Watch for.** A compliance-mode lock cannot be shortened, even by
administrators; test retention on a non-production bucket first.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Object storage](#object-storage) ·
[Zero trust](#zero-trust) ·
[Private cloud](#private-cloud)

</p>

[Read the source · Amazon S3 · Object
Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock.html)

[Link to this definition](#object-lock)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="object-storage"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## Object storage {#object-storage}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

Storage that keeps whole objects with metadata in flat buckets, addressed by
key through an HTTP API.

**In practice.** Keep Parquet files and table metadata in an S3-compatible
bucket that several engines share.

**Watch for.** S3 compatibility varies by feature: conditional writes,
versioning, object lock and listing behavior must be tested.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse) ·
[Private cloud](#private-cloud) ·
[Object Lock (WORM)](#object-lock)

</p>

[Read the source · Amazon S3 · user
guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html)

[Link to this definition](#object-storage)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="observability"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Observability {#observability}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

The ability to understand a system from the outside, through the traces,
metrics and logs it emits, including problems nobody anticipated.

**In practice.** Follow a slow request's trace from the API to the query that
caused the delay.

**Watch for.** More telemetry is not more understanding; cardinality, sampling
and retention decide cost and which questions stay answerable.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Site reliability engineering (SRE)](#sre) ·
[AIOps](#aiops) ·
[Error budget](#error-budget) ·
[OpenTelemetry](#opentelemetry)

</p>

[Read the source · OpenTelemetry · observability
primer](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/observability-primer/)

[Link to this definition](#observability)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="olap"
data-category="data" markdown>

## OLAP {#olap}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Online analytical processing: queries that scan and aggregate many rows over
few columns, usually served by columnar storage and vectorized execution.

**In practice.** Aggregate a year of events by region to refresh a dashboard.

**Watch for.** Fast scans do not make an engine good at frequent point
updates, transactions or high-concurrency writes.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[ClickHouse](#clickhouse) ·
[DuckDB](#duckdb) ·
[Query federation](#query-federation) ·
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse)

</p>

OLAP?](https://clickhouse.com/resources/engineering/what-is-olap)

[Link to this definition](#olap)

[Try it: Group and aggregate rows](projects/tools.md#interactive-sql-sandbox)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="open-table-format"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Open table format {#open-table-format}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

A specification that turns data files in object storage into tables with
snapshots, schema and partition metadata that several engines can share.

**In practice.** Spark writes an Iceberg table that Trino and DuckDB query
through the same catalog.

**Watch for.** Engines support different spec versions and features; sharing a
format still requires a shared catalog and tested writers.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse) ·
[Object storage](#object-storage) ·
[Schema evolution](#schema-evolution) ·
[Query federation](#query-federation) ·
[DuckDB](#duckdb) ·
[Table catalog](#table-catalog)

</p>

[Read the source · Apache Iceberg · table
spec](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/)

[Link to this definition](#open-table-format)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="opentelemetry"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## OpenTelemetry {#opentelemetry}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

An open standard, with SDKs and a collector, for producing traces, metrics and
logs that share context and naming conventions, exported over OTLP.

**In practice.** A request's trace ID follows it from the API through the
queue to the worker, so the one slow step shows up end to end.

**Watch for.** It standardizes how signals are collected, not where they are
stored or alerted on; sampling and label cardinality still decide the cost.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Observability](#observability) ·
[Site reliability engineering (SRE)](#sre) ·
[Tail latency (p95/p99)](#tail-latency) ·
[LLMOps](#llmops)

</p>

[Read the source · OpenTelemetry · What is
OpenTelemetry?](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/what-is-opentelemetry/)

[Link to this definition](#opentelemetry)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="prefill-decode"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Prefill and decode {#prefill-decode}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

The two phases of LLM inference: prefill processes the prompt in parallel and
is compute-bound; decode generates one token at a time and is memory-bound.

**In practice.** Serve long prompts on prefill workers and hand their KV cache
to decode workers over a fast interconnect.

**Watch for.** Disaggregation adds KV transfer and scheduling cost; it pays
off only for some prompt lengths, output lengths and latency targets.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[KV cache](#kv-cache) ·
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Mixture of experts (MoE)](#mixture-of-experts) ·
[LLMOps](#llmops)

</p>

[Read the source · Zhong et al., DistServe, OSDI
2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670)

[Link to this definition](#prefill-decode)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="private-cloud"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## Private cloud {#private-cloud}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

Cloud resources dedicated to one organization, whether operated on its
premises or by a provider.

**In practice.** An internal platform offers self-service environments to
several business units.

**Watch for.** Virtual machines alone do not establish a cloud operating
model.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[VPC](#vpc) ·
[Landing zone](#landing-zone) ·
[Infrastructure as code](#iac) ·
[FinOps](#finops)

</p>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="quantization"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Quantization {#quantization}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Represent selected model values with lower precision to reduce storage and
potentially computation.

**In practice.** Evaluate 4-bit weights against the original model using a
held-out workload.

**Watch for.** Smaller weights do not guarantee faster inference or unchanged
quality; hardware support matters, and published checkpoints often keep
sensitive layers in BF16.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[KV cache](#kv-cache) ·
[Mixture of experts (MoE)](#mixture-of-experts) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation) ·
[LLMOps](#llmops)

</p>

Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/quantization/overview)

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="query-federation"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Query federation {#query-federation}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Querying several data sources from one SQL engine through connectors, without
first copying the data into that engine's storage.

**In practice.** Trino joins an Iceberg table with a PostgreSQL reference
table in one query.

**Watch for.** Speed depends on what each connector can push down; federation
still loads the sources and does not reconcile their consistency.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[OLAP](#olap) ·
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse) ·
[ClickHouse](#clickhouse)

</p>

[Read the source · Trino ·
connectors](https://trino.io/docs/current/connector.html)

[Link to this definition](#query-federation)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="rag"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## RAG {#rag}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Generation conditioned on information retrieved from an external collection,
rather than model parameters alone.

**In practice.** Retrieve relevant policy passages and provide them as context
for an answer.

**Watch for.** Retrieval can miss evidence; supplied context does not
guarantee a supported answer.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Vector search](#vector-search) ·
[AI agent](#agent) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation) ·
[LLMOps](#llmops) ·

</p>

2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

[Link to this definition](#rag)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="schema-evolution"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Schema evolution {#schema-evolution}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Changing a table or message schema while stating which existing readers and
writers keep working.

**In practice.** Adding an optional column keeps current readers working;
dropping a required one breaks them.

**Watch for.** Compatibility in one direction does not imply the other; a
rename is a removal plus an addition unless the format tracks column IDs.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[Change data capture](#cdc) ·
[Data lineage](#lineage) ·
[dbt](#dbt)

</p>

evolution](https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/evolution/)

[Link to this definition](#schema-evolution)

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="sre"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Site reliability engineering (SRE) {#sre}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

Apply software engineering to operating services with explicit reliability
goals and limited manual toil.

**In practice.** Use an error budget to decide whether to ship a change or
address reliability first.

**Watch for.** Reliability targets reflect user needs and cost; a dashboard
alone is not an SRE practice.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Error budget](#error-budget) ·
[Observability](#observability) ·
[DevOps](#devops) ·
[AIOps](#aiops)

</p>

[Read the source · Google SRE ·
introduction](https://sre.google/sre-book/introduction/)

[Link to this definition](#sre)

[Try it: Calculate an error budget](projects/tools.md#interactive-slo-budget)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="slo"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## SLO {#slo}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

A target for a measured service indicator, over a defined population and time
window.

**In practice.** At least 99.9% of valid requests succeed over a rolling
30-day window.

**Watch for.** A target is not a measurement or a contractual guarantee;
exclusions must be explicit.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Error budget](#error-budget) ·
[Site reliability engineering (SRE)](#sre) ·
[Observability](#observability) ·
[Backoff](#backoff) ·
[Circuit breaker](#circuit-breaker) ·

</p>

[Read the source · Google
SRE](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/)

[Link to this definition](#slo)

[Try it: Calculate an error budget](projects/tools.md#interactive-slo-budget)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="streaming"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Streaming {#streaming}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

Process events as a continuing flow, with explicit rules for time, state and
late arrivals.

**In practice.** Update available inventory as order events arrive.

**Watch for.** Low latency still requires replay, backpressure and duplicate
handling; it does not mean instant or lossless.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Batch processing](#batch) ·
[Watermark](#watermark) ·
[Apache Kafka](#kafka) ·
[Compaction](#compaction)

</p>

time](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-stable/docs/concepts/time/)

[Link to this definition](#streaming)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="table-catalog"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Table catalog {#table-catalog}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

The service that maps a table name to its current metadata and makes each
commit atomic, so every engine sees the same table state.

**In practice.** Spark writes analytics.orders and Trino reads it through the
same REST catalog, so the new snapshot is visible to both.

**Watch for.** A shared bucket without a shared catalog is not a shared table:
engines must speak the same catalog protocol and honor its permissions.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[Lakehouse](#lakehouse) ·
[Query federation](#query-federation) ·
[Table snapshot and time travel](#snapshot)

</p>

[Read the source · Apache Iceberg · REST catalog
specification](https://iceberg.apache.org/rest-catalog-spec/)

[Link to this definition](#table-catalog)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="snapshot"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Table snapshot and time travel {#snapshot}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

An immutable version of a table's state after a commit; a query can read an
older snapshot by its ID or timestamp.

**In practice.** Compare today's revenue with the table as it was before last
night's backfill.

**Watch for.** Old snapshots keep their files on storage until they expire, so
retention is a cost and compliance decision.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Open table format](#open-table-format) ·
[Compaction](#compaction) ·
[Backfill](#backfill) ·
[Table catalog](#table-catalog)

</p>

[Read the source · Apache Iceberg · time travel
queries](https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-queries/#time-travel)

[Link to this definition](#snapshot)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="tail-latency"
data-category="platform" markdown>

## Tail latency (p95/p99) {#tail-latency}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Platform</p>

The response time that only the slowest few percent of requests exceed, such
as the 99th percentile.

**In practice.** An API averages 80 ms, but its p99 is 1.2 s: one request in a
hundred waits more than a second.

**Watch for.** Percentiles cannot be averaged across servers or time windows;
aggregate the underlying histograms instead.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[SLO](#slo) ·
[Error budget](#error-budget) ·
[Observability](#observability) ·
[Prefill and decode](#prefill-decode)

</p>

[Read the source · Google SRE · Service level
objectives](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/)

[Link to this definition](#tail-latency)

[Try it: Query p99 latency in sample runs](projects/tools.md#interactive-sql-sandbox)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="vector-search"
data-category="ai" markdown>

## Vector search {#vector-search}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">AI</p>

Retrieval that ranks items by the similarity of their embeddings, numeric
vectors a model produces from text, images or other data.

**In practice.** Find policy passages close in meaning to a question even when
they share no keywords.

**Watch for.** Approximate indexes trade recall for speed; exact identifiers,
filters and freshness often need hybrid keyword search.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[RAG](#rag) ·
[Evaluation](#evaluation) ·
[AI agent](#agent) ·
[Embedding](#embedding)

</p>

HNSW](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320)

[Link to this definition](#vector-search)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="vpc"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## VPC {#vpc}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

A logically isolated virtual network in a cloud provider, with controlled
addressing and connectivity.

**In practice.** Separate application subnets from a database subnet and
define their routes.

**Watch for.** A VPC is a network boundary, not proof of complete workload
isolation.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Private cloud](#private-cloud) ·
[Zero trust](#zero-trust) ·
[Landing zone](#landing-zone) ·

</p>

VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/what-is-amazon-vpc.html)

[Link to this definition](#vpc)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="watermark"
data-category="data" markdown>

## Watermark {#watermark}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Data</p>

A stream-processing signal of event-time progress, used to decide when
time-based operations can advance.

**In practice.** Close a window after its watermark passes the window end,
with a policy for late events.

**Watch for.** A watermark is not a guarantee that no older event will ever
arrive.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[Streaming](#streaming) ·
[Apache Kafka](#kafka) ·
[Change data capture](#cdc)

</p>

[Read the source · Apache
Flink](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-stable/docs/concepts/time/)

[Link to this definition](#watermark)

</section>

<section class="glossary-entry" data-term-id="zero-trust"
data-category="cloud" markdown>

## Zero trust {#zero-trust}

<p class="glossary-entry-domain">Cloud</p>

A security model that authorizes each request from verified identity, device
and context instead of trusting network location.

**In practice.** A service reaches a database only with a short-lived workload
identity, even inside the same VPC.

**Watch for.** Zero trust is an architecture adopted incrementally, not a
product; legacy paths often keep implicit trust.

<p class="glossary-related" markdown>

**Related concepts:**
[VPC](#vpc) ·
[DevSecOps](#devsecops) ·
[Landing zone](#landing-zone) ·
[Private cloud](#private-cloud)

</p>

[Read the source · NIST SP
800-207](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final)

[Link to this definition](#zero-trust)

      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#airflow",
      "name": "Apache Airflow",
      "description": "Coordinate workflows defined as code, including dependencies, schedules, retries and task state.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#kafka",
      "name": "Apache Kafka",
      "description": "A distributed event-streaming platform with partitioned logs that producers write and consumers can replay.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#backfill",
      "name": "Backfill",
      "description": "Recomputing or loading data for a past period, for example after fixing a transformation or adding a column.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#backoff",
      "name": "Backoff",
      "description": "Delay successive retries to reduce pressure on a failing dependency; jitter spreads synchronized clients.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#batch",
      "name": "Batch processing",
      "description": "Process a bounded collection of data as a job, rather than treating it as an endless flow.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#cdc",
      "name": "Change data capture",
      "description": "Turn database changes into events that downstream consumers can process incrementally.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#circuit-breaker",
      "name": "Circuit breaker",
      "description": "Temporarily stop calls after enough failures, then admit limited probes to check recovery.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#clickhouse",
      "name": "ClickHouse",
      "description": "A column-oriented SQL database designed for analytical queries over large volumes of data.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#compaction",
      "name": "Compaction",
      "description": "Rewriting many small data files into fewer files near a target size, without changing the table's rows.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#lineage",
      "name": "Data lineage",
      "description": "Recorded relationships between datasets, jobs and runs that explain where data came from and how it changed.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#dataops",
      "name": "DataOps",
      "description": "Collaborative practices that improve delivery and operation of analytical data through automation, testing and feedback.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#dbt",
      "name": "dbt",
      "description": "Build, test and document data transformations from versioned models and their dependencies.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#dlq",
      "name": "Dead-letter queue",
      "description": "A separate destination for messages that could not be processed within the configured attempt limit.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#devops",
      "name": "DevOps",
      "description": "Shared practices and responsibility across software delivery and operation, supported by automation and feedback.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#devsecops",
      "name": "DevSecOps",
      "description": "Integrate security practices and shared responsibility throughout software development, delivery and operation.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#duckdb",
      "name": "DuckDB",
      "description": "An analytical SQL engine that can run inside an application and query files such as Parquet.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#durable-execution",
      "name": "Durable execution",
      "description": "Workflow execution whose progress is recorded, so it resumes after crashes, deployments or long waits without repeating completed steps.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#embedding",
      "name": "Embedding",
      "description": "A fixed-length vector that a model assigns to text, images or other data, so that similar meaning ends up close together.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#error-budget",
      "name": "Error budget",
      "description": "The unreliability an SLO allows over its window: one minus the target, applied to eligible requests or measured time.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#evaluation",
      "name": "Evaluation",
      "description": "A defined set of tasks and scoring rules used to inspect system behavior, including failures.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#finops",
      "name": "FinOps",
      "description": "Shared practices connecting technology spending, ownership and business value through engineering, finance and product collaboration.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#gitops",
      "name": "GitOps",
      "description": "Continuous reconciliation of running systems against a versioned description of their intended state.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#hybrid-attention",
      "name": "Hybrid attention",
      "description": "A model design that interleaves full-attention layers with linear-attention layers whose recurrent state does not grow with context.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#idempotency",
      "name": "Idempotency",
      "description": "Repeating the same operation has the same intended effect as performing it once.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#iac",
      "name": "Infrastructure as code",
      "description": "Infrastructure definitions stored as reviewable, versioned configuration that automation can apply.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#kv-cache",
      "name": "KV cache",
      "description": "Stored attention keys and values from prior tokens, reused during autoregressive decoding.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#lakehouse",
      "name": "Lakehouse",
      "description": "An analytical architecture combining lake-style storage with table management and warehouse-style capabilities.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#landing-zone",
      "name": "Landing zone",
      "description": "A prepared multi-account or multi-project cloud environment with baseline identity, networking, logging and security guardrails for new workloads.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#llmops",
      "name": "LLMOps",
      "description": "Lifecycle practices for releasing, evaluating and operating applications built around language models.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#mcp",
      "name": "MCP",
      "description": "A protocol through which AI applications discover and interact with tools, resources and prompts exposed by servers.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#medallion",
      "name": "Medallion architecture",
      "description": "Organize data by refinement: bronze retains raw input, silver validates it and gold serves a use case.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#mixture-of-experts",
      "name": "Mixture of experts (MoE)",
      "description": "A model layer that routes each token to a few expert sub-networks, so only part of the parameters computes each token.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#mlops",
      "name": "MLOps",
      "description": "Practices for delivering and operating ML systems across code, data, training, deployment and monitoring.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#multi-agent",
      "name": "Multi-agent systems",
      "description": "Several agents cooperate with distinct responsibilities, context or permissions in one workflow.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#object-lock",
      "name": "Object Lock (WORM)",
      "description": "A storage setting that makes an object version immutable for a retention period: write once, read many.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#object-storage",
      "name": "Object storage",
      "description": "Storage that keeps whole objects with metadata in flat buckets, addressed by key through an HTTP API.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#observability",
      "name": "Observability",
      "description": "The ability to understand a system from the outside, through the traces, metrics and logs it emits, including problems nobody anticipated.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#olap",
      "name": "OLAP",
      "description": "Online analytical processing: queries that scan and aggregate many rows over few columns, usually served by columnar storage and vectorized execution.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#open-table-format",
      "name": "Open table format",
      "description": "A specification that turns data files in object storage into tables with snapshots, schema and partition metadata that several engines can share.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#opentelemetry",
      "name": "OpenTelemetry",
      "description": "An open standard, with SDKs and a collector, for producing traces, metrics and logs that share context and naming conventions, exported over OTLP.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#prefill-decode",
      "name": "Prefill and decode",
      "description": "The two phases of LLM inference: prefill processes the prompt in parallel and is compute-bound; decode generates one token at a time and is memory-bound.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#private-cloud",
      "name": "Private cloud",
      "description": "Cloud resources dedicated to one organization, whether operated on its premises or by a provider.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#quantization",
      "name": "Quantization",
      "description": "Represent selected model values with lower precision to reduce storage and potentially computation.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#query-federation",
      "name": "Query federation",
      "description": "Querying several data sources from one SQL engine through connectors, without first copying the data into that engine's storage.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#rag",
      "name": "RAG",
      "description": "Generation conditioned on information retrieved from an external collection, rather than model parameters alone.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#schema-evolution",
      "name": "Schema evolution",
      "description": "Changing a table or message schema while stating which existing readers and writers keep working.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#sre",
      "name": "Site reliability engineering (SRE)",
      "description": "Apply software engineering to operating services with explicit reliability goals and limited manual toil.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#slo",
      "name": "SLO",
      "description": "A target for a measured service indicator, over a defined population and time window.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#streaming",
      "name": "Streaming",
      "description": "Process events as a continuing flow, with explicit rules for time, state and late arrivals.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#table-catalog",
      "name": "Table catalog",
      "description": "The service that maps a table name to its current metadata and makes each commit atomic, so every engine sees the same table state.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#snapshot",
      "name": "Table snapshot and time travel",
      "description": "An immutable version of a table's state after a commit; a query can read an older snapshot by its ID or timestamp.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#tail-latency",
      "name": "Tail latency (p95/p99)",
      "description": "The response time that only the slowest few percent of requests exceed, such as the 99th percentile.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#vector-search",
      "name": "Vector search",
      "description": "Retrieval that ranks items by the similarity of their embeddings, numeric vectors a model produces from text, images or other data.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#vpc",
      "name": "VPC",
      "description": "A logically isolated virtual network in a cloud provider, with controlled addressing and connectivity.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#watermark",
      "name": "Watermark",
      "description": "A stream-processing signal of event-time progress, used to decide when time-based operations can advance.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    },
    {
      "@type": "DefinedTerm",
      "@id": "https://landerox.com/glossary/#zero-trust",
      "name": "Zero trust",
      "description": "A security model that authorizes each request from verified identity, device and context instead of trusting network location.",
      "inDefinedTermSet": "https://landerox.com/glossary/"
    }
  ]
}
</script>
